nodes.label: rdev::listen is X11-only and does not work on Wayland
nodes.norm_label: rdev::listen is x11-only and does not work on wayland
nodes.rationale: The report quotes the crate's own documentation and the released feature set that still ships no Wayland backend: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08166] The listen function uses X11 APIs, and so will not work in Wayland or in the linux kernel virtual console"* [1]. So `rdev::listen` is a hard no on the target machine, and the silent-failure path is exactly what `rdev_hook.rs:153-155` logs. Only the unstable `grab` (evdev-based) claims Wayland support, and even that requires membership in the `input` group [1]. Upstream is aware: issue #82 "Any plans for wayland support?" was closed without landing a Wayland `listen` [3], issue #116 proposes switching the Linux backend to libinput and remains open [4], and PR #191 adds a `wayland` feature flag with runtime backend selection — still open, and 0.5.3 ships only `serialize` and `unstable_grab` features [2][5], so nothing here is reachable in a released version.

nodes.label: The XDG RemoteDesktop portal is injection-only and can never produce counts
nodes.norm_label: the xdg remotedesktop portal is injection-only and can never produce counts
nodes.rationale: Why the RemoteDesktop portal can never yield counts, in the report's own words: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08168] portal is *injection only*: its entire API is `NotifyPointerMotion`, `NotifyKeyboardKeycode`, `NotifyTouchDown`, etc., plus `ConnectToEIS` for a *sender* libei context [7]. There is no read-back channel, so it can never produce counts.

nodes.label: XDG InputCapture is trigger-based, so it is not a global telemetry feed
nodes.norm_label: xdg inputcapture is trigger-based, so it is not a global telemetry feed
nodes.rationale: Why InputCapture is not a telemetry feed, in the report's own words: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08168] Input capturing is trigger-based. Currently the only defined trigger is pointer barriers"*, *"The compositor is always in control of input capturing and may filter events or stop capturing at any time"*, and events flow only when the compositor emits `Activated` after a barrier is crossed [8]. It is a game/streaming anti-cheat and remote-control API, not a global telemetry feed. KDE does implement it (Arch Wiki marks Input Capture "Yes" for `xdg-desktop-portal-kde` [9], implemented from KDE issue #12), but even if fully wired it would deliver counts only while the cursor is crossing a barrier, which is useless for activity density.

nodes.label: libinput and libseat grant no privilege advantage over raw evdev
nodes.norm_label: libinput and libseat grant no privilege advantage over raw evdev
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08172] `libinput` / `libseat`.** No privilege advantage. libinput "only supports evdev devices" and maintains "a 1:1 mapping between libinput devices and `/dev/input/eventX` device nodes" [11]; `libseat`/`seatd` are seat-managers that grant *the same* device access, not a lesser one.

nodes.label: XTest and xdotool cannot observe native Wayland client input through XWayland
nodes.norm_label: xtest and xdotool cannot observe native wayland client input through xwayland
nodes.rationale: Why XTest and xdotool cannot see native Wayland client input: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08174] XTest synthesises events into the X server and only observes X11 input; native Wayland clients' input never traverses XWayland. xdotool's README is unambiguous: *"If you are using Wayland, please be aware this software will not work correctly... Typing, window searching, and many other functions of xdotool do not work, and it is unclear if they could ever work"* [12]. This is also why global shortcuts on Wayland require a portal at all.

nodes.label: Wayland input density availability
nodes.rationale: Availability is gated on a grant the report calls keylogger-equivalent, and the session must surface it instead of degrading silently: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08170] Critically, **out of the box neither applies**: Arch Wiki carries an explicit warning — *"Do not set the `uaccess` tag on input or block devices; those have their own access control mechanisms and unprivileged users should not have raw access to those. For instance, unprivileged raw keyboard access would make keylogging trivial"* [10]. So a KDE Plasma Wayland session does **not** hand `/dev/input/event*` to an ordinary app; Snipset's existing `evdev_hook.rs` already models this with `EVDEV_STATE_NO_PERMISSION` and the `input` group is a documented prerequisite in the Wayland backend plan. The security implication is real and unavoidable: this permission is equivalent to keylogger access, and the project must justify it as a deliberate, user-granted, opt-in capability. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08194] Snipset must present it as an explicit opt-in with a visible permission state, never silently degrade to zero counts, and never read or persist keycodes beyond the aggregate counters.

nodes.label: Linux capture provider input-density gate
nodes.rationale: No new capture mechanism: the counters are already running, and the report names both the missing read and the branch that hardcodes the field away: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08162] And the critical finding for this repo is that the mechanism is **already running and already populating the counters** — the only missing piece is the single `#[cfg]` read in `capture_provider.rs`. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - deep-research-wayland-input-density [ses_f258b313affeq5eT2xP5hKvAjA].md:L08190] The `input_density: None` at `capture_provider.rs:158` is the entire defect: a Linux-only branch hardcodes the field to `None` while the read block at line 91 sits behind `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]`.

nodes.rationale: The instrument was indicted rather than the machine, and every earlier wattage figure was withdrawn on that basis: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-27 - efisiensi-daya-listrik-pc [ses_f1d988394ffeR7mzol16F72rHi].md:L02726] Suhu naik 27°C itu CPU working keras. RAPL tetap datar. Jadi RAPL di mesin ini **under-report parah**. Kontrol positif gagal → sesuai aturan sendiri, **methods-nya yang salah, bukan sistemnya**. Konsekuensi: semua angka "idle 0,4–2,5 W" dan "beban 47 W" yang gue tulis sebelumnya **ngawur**, hapus dari ingatan.

Jadi gue bisa bedain crash dari shutdown biasa. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-27 - efisiensi-daya-listrik-pc [ses_f1d988394ffeR7mzol16F72rHi].md:L05963] ## Yang sudah ruled out (dengan bukti) [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-27 - efisiensi-daya-listrik-pc [ses_f1d988394ffeR7mzol16F72rHi].md:L05982] **Nolnya yang aneh.** Load normal, RAM masih 3,3 GB free, 48°C, PSI ~0. Tool lu bekerja persis desainnya — dan kesimpulannya "tidak ada yang salah sebelum mati." Itu negative result yang benar, bukan data jelek.
